name: Em Essex
description:
'''Em Essex''' (also known as '''em''', '''msx''', '''Renard Queenston''', and many other [[pseudonym]]s) is a Canadian [[electronic music]]ian and [[video game developer]]. They{{efn|Essex is [[agender]] and uses ''it/they'' [[personal pronouns]].<ref group="‡" name="msx"/> This article uses ''[[they/them]]'' for consistency.}} have operated the [[netlabel]] LapFox Trax and the record label and studio Halley Labs.

Essex's aliases are represented by [[original character]]s, largely [[anthropomorphic]] animals, and correspond to different musical styles or genres. Their work includes [[breakcore]], [[glitch (music)|glitch]], [[chiptune]], [[happy hardcore]], and [[speedcore]]. An active member of the [[furry fandom]], Essex has performed as a DJ at [[Anthrocon]].

"Rubber Band", which was released under the Jackal Queenston alias, became associated with the "'''penis music'''" [[Internet meme]] in 2019. Essex also created ''End of Starchild'', a standalone game built with [[GZDoom]] and a sequel to ''Time Tripper'' (2021). The game combines [[first-person shooter]] and [[bullet hell]] mechanics and includes a separate [[role-playing video game|role-playing game]].
